thread:
olivia: Hi all — I'm Olivia, started on runtime today. Trying to build the runtime from source on my dev laptop (Ubuntu 22.04). The cmake pass finishes but the link fails with a weird nvcc/ld error. Any pointers?

olivia: Paste of the end of the log:```\n[ 86%] Linking CXX executable bin/runtime_server\n/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart_static.a(libcudart_static.a.o): relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against symbol `__cudaRegisterLinkedBinary' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC\ncollect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status\n```\n
paige: welcome Olivia :wave: quick q — did you install CUDA from deb (apt) or the runfile?

olivia: runfile installer, then symlinked /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1. I also changed alternatives to gcc-11 locally.

paige: OK. That error usually means some static CUDA libs were built without -fPIC and you're linking them into a shared target. Two quick things:
- try building with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF (if ok for dev) or add -fPIC to CXX_FLAGS
- also check ccache: stale objects can hide ABI mismatches

jakob: fwiw we normally recommend using the distro's CUDA package image or our devcontainer to avoid local toolchain weirdness. If you want to stay local:
```\nexport CC=/usr/bin/gcc-11\nexport CXX=/usr/bin/g++-11\ncmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON\ncmake --build build -j$(nproc)\n```\n
olivia: tried with explicit CC/CXX but same linker complaint. I noticed ccache is enabled on my machine. Could that cause mixing of old objects?

jakob: yes. Try clearing ccache: `ccache -C` then rebuild. Or temporarily disable: `export CCACHE_DISABLE=1` then cmake clean.

olivia: did ccache -C and a full clean. New run hits a different error from nvcc:```\nptxas fatal : Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_86'\nerror: command '/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas' failed with exit status 255\n```\n
paige: that means the CUDA toolkit you're using doesn't recognize the compute capability flag the build expects. Which GPU target is set in your env? Check `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` or env `CUDA_ARCH`.

olivia: I didn't set it explicitly; cmake summary shows `CUDA_ARCH=86` coming from the repo default. My laptop is an RTX A2000 (sm_86) but toolkit is 12.1 installed from runfile.

paige: weird — CUDA 12 should support sm_86 generally, but runfile installer sometimes leaves an older ptxas in PATH if you have multiple toolkits. `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version`?

olivia: `which ptxas` -> `/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas` ; `ptxas --version` -> reports CUDA 11.4. I think I had an older toolkit leftover in /usr/local/cuda-11.4/bin and PATH order is wrong.

jakob: yep that's it. Either update PATH to point to /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin first or remove the old symlink. Also check LD_LIBRARY_PATH for libcuda and the linker picking correct libs.

olivia: quickfix worked: updated PATH to put /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin first, cleared ccache, reconfigured, and now linking past that point. :tada: Still seeing one warning about PIC on a third-party static lib — probably fine for dev, but we should call it out.

paige: great! If you want, open a short PR in infra/devcontainers to add an environment check script that validates ptxas and nvcc versions. We've bitten by mixed toolchain paths before.

olivia: will do. thanks for the help y'all. Also, @infra-bot any chance of a fresh devcontainer image with cuda-12.1 pinned? My laptop setup is messy.

infra-bot: queued image build for tag `devcontainer-cuda-12.1` — will post link on completion.

buildkite: Build queued: https://buildkite.com/redwood/runtime-devcontainers/builds/4521 (infra team)

jakob: quick note for onboarding checklist: add a step to verify `ptxas --version` and `which ptxas` — saves 30 mins usually.

olivia: adding that to my onboarding notes. Thanks again! :heart:
